questionText: Partners Amit and Sumit entered into a partnership without executing a partnership deed. Amit contributed Rs. 10,00,000 whereas Sumit contributed Rs. 2,00,000. At year end, how should the net profit be shared?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

chapter: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm: Admission, Retirement and Death
topic: Change in PSR: Sacrificing and Gaining Share
questionText: In Partnership Firm #1, partners A and B share profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. They mutually agree to share future profits equally (1:1). What is the sacrifice or gain of each partner?

options.text: Partner A sacrifices 1/10 and Partner B gains 1/10
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

options.text: Partner A gains 1/10 and Partner B sacrifices 1/10
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Partner A gains 1/10 and Partner B sacrifices 1/10'.

options.text: Both Partner A and Partner B sacrifice 1/10
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Both Partner A and Partner B sacrifice 1/10'.
Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Neither partner sacrifices or gains'.

detailedSolution:
1. Formula: Sacrificing Share = Old Share - New Share.
   - Partner A's Share = (3/5) - (1/2) = (6 - 5)/10 = 1/10 (Sacrifice).
   - Partner B's Share = (2/5) - (1/2) = (4 - 5)/10 = -1/10 (Gain).
2. Therefore, Partner A sacrifices 1/10 and Partner B gains 1/10.
Hence, Option A is correct.

chapter: Dissolution of a Partnership Firm
questionText: On dissolution of Firm #1: Realisation expenses of Rs. 5,000 were to be borne by the firm and were paid by the firm. What is the journal entry in the firm's books?

options.text: Realisation A/c Dr. to Cash/Bank A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

options.text: Partner's Capital A/c Dr. to Cash/Bank A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Partner's Capital A/c Dr. to Cash/Bank A/c'.

options.text: Cash/Bank A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Cash/Bank A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c'.
Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'No entry is required'.

detailedSolution:
1. Accounting Treatment of Dissolution Expenses:
   - When expenses are borne by firm and paid by firm -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Bank A/c.
   - When borne by partner and paid by firm -> Partner's Capital A/c Dr. to Bank A/c.
   - When borne by partner and paid by partner personally -> No entry in firm's books.
   - When borne by firm and paid by partner -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Partner's Capital A/c.
   - Remuneration allowed to partner -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Partner's Capital A/c.
Hence, Option A is correct.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

options.text: D's Capital A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'D's Capital A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c'.

options.text: D's Capital A/c Dr. to Bank A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'D's Capital A/c Dr. to Bank A/c'.

options.text: Bank A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Bank A/c Dr. to Realisation A/c'.

detailedSolution:
1. Accounting Treatment of Dissolution Expenses:
   - When expenses are borne by firm and paid by firm -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Bank A/c.
   - When borne by partner and paid by firm -> Partner's Capital A/c Dr. to Bank A/c.
   - When borne by partner and paid by partner personally -> No entry in firm's books.
   - When borne by firm and paid by partner -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Partner's Capital A/c.
   - Remuneration allowed to partner -> Realisation A/c Dr. to Partner's Capital A/c.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In corporate legal compliance case #3: Under Section 52(2) of the Companies Act, 2013, Securities Premium CANNOT be utilized for which of the following purposes?

options.text: Issuing fully paid bonus shares to existing shareholders
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Issuing fully paid bonus shares to existing shareholders'.

options.text: Writing off preliminary expenses of the company
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Writing off preliminary expenses of the company'.

options.text: Distribution of cash dividends to equity shareholders
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Conforms to standard NCERT Accountancy principles and accounting standards.

options.text: Providing premium payable on redemption of debentures or preference shares
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Providing premium payable on redemption of debentures or preference shares'.

detailedSolution:
1. Section 52(2) strictly restricts the application of Securities Premium to 5 specific purposes:
   (i) Bonus shares, (ii) Preliminary expenses, (iii) Issue expenses/commission/discount on shares/debentures, (iv) Premium on redemption of debentures/preference shares, (v) Buy-back of shares.
   - It CANNOT be used to pay dividends to shareholders.
Hence, Option C is correct.
